s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Hemosiderotic fibrohistiocytic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition, and is supported by pathology findings of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells positive for CD34

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic hyalinizing angiectatic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Shares some histological features with the case, including spindled and epithelioid cells, and could present as a subcutaneous mass

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the presence of spindled cells and mature adipose tissue in the pathology, although the clinical context is less typical

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Is a rare tumor that could present with similar clinical and histological features, including a subcutaneous mass with pigment deposition

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although typically involves the synovium, its histological features of pigmented villonodular synovitis could be considered in the differential diagnosis of a subcutaneous lesion with pigment deposition
